project.title: Nothing Personal
project.maker: Natasha Jen and team at Pentagram for Mozilla Foundation
project.medium: digital editorial platform and magazine identity
project.format: Responsive editorial site with feature stories, product reviews, advice, and podcast content

why: A useful contemporary editorial reference because it treats the browser as part of the publication's visual language: the identity can feel like a magazine, a web page, and a conversation with internet culture at the same time.

readingRhythm.title: One strong thesis before the index
readingRhythm.study: The official platform places a large editorial proposition and featured story material before the supporting review, humor, and podcast sections.
readingRhythm.reuse: Give a publication landing page one unmistakable point of view before exposing the full archive or content taxonomy.

readingRhythm.title: Mix deep reads with utility beats
readingRhythm.study: Feature stories, technology product reviews, advice, and audio content sit in adjacent but distinct content modes.
readingRhythm.reuse: Use different content lengths and tones as pacing devices, while keeping shared labels and framing consistent enough to feel like one issue.

compositions.title: Web vernacular as editorial framing
compositions.study: The credited case study describes a visual language borrowing from pop-ups, chat windows, and browser bars, treating interruption as part of the publication's human mark.
compositions.reuse: Turn familiar interface containers into editorial punctuation for stories about technology, culture, or the networked world.

compositions.title: A mark that behaves, not just identifies
compositions.study: The NP. mark is described as deliberately simple and able to overlay imagery as both a window and a veil.
compositions.reuse: Design an editorial mark with placement behavior and an expressive relationship to imagery, rather than limiting it to the masthead.

compositions.title: Contrast creates the cover energy
compositions.study: The platform uses direct headlines, people-centered editorial subjects, and a strong contrast between content modes to establish a magazine-like front door.
compositions.reuse: Let the first screen establish editorial attitude through scale, contrast, and a single story signal before the archive becomes visible.

typeImageSystems.notes: The case study describes a large, direct, slightly awkward typographic voice built on Mozilla's type family.
typeImageSystems.reuse: Use a deliberately human display voice against a quieter reading face so the publication can shift from headline attitude to sustained reading.

typeImageSystems.notes: The visual system combines bright contrast, solid blocks, borders, and framing devices with photography or illustration.
typeImageSystems.reuse: Treat image treatment, color fields, and framing as interchangeable layers so each story can have a distinct image while retaining the same publication grammar.

assets.notes: The source case describes solid blocks and borders as compositional punctuation; this library recreates the principle with original CSS only.
assets.reuse: Build a small set of shapes and borders that can frame stories, reviews, and calls to action without copying the source identity.

assets.notes: The external NP. mark is proprietary and is not included in the local preview.
assets.reuse: Use an original editorial mark with a similarly behavioral role when prototyping; do not reproduce the source mark.

implementation.format: Responsive web editorial platform with magazine-like hierarchy and mixed media entry points
implementation.notes: The official Mozilla platform verifies the content modes and editorial positioning. The credited case study supplies the visual grammar; implementation details are intentionally limited to observed composition and reuse principles.
